top_stories.title: OpenAI slashes GPT-5.6 API prices as competition bites
points: GPT-5.6 Luna input tokens dropped 80% to $0.20 per million and output 60% to $1.20 per million (tokens are the chunks of text an AI model reads and writes; API pricing is billed per million of them).
GPT-5.6 Terra fell to $2 per million input and $12 per million output — reported as a 75%/40% cut by TLDR and a 20% cut by The Code and Techpresso.
GPT-5.6 Sol pricing unchanged, though a faster Sol variant was added to the API.
Cuts come as enterprise buyers grow cost-sensitive and cheaper Chinese open-weight models (models whose parameters are freely downloadable) undercut OpenAI.
The Luna cut landed just 21 days after the model launched, on July 30.

unique_angles.point: Auto-review in the ChatGPT app and Codex CLI was upgraded from GPT-5.4 to GPT-5.6 Luna, making everyday AI code review cheaper and faster.
OpenAI credited efficiency gains including Sol rewriting production kernels to cut serving costs 20%, but offered no independent verification and no disclosure of the impact on its 33% gross margin.
Frames the move as a direct fight with Anthropic's Claude for developer workloads.

top_stories.title: Tesla weighs separating China business to clear a SpaceX merger
points: Tesla executives were told to prepare options to spin off, sell, or shut down the China unit, per a Wall Street Journal report.
SpaceX's large U.S. defense contracts would trigger heavy national-security scrutiny if merged with a company holding Chinese operations.
Tesla's Chinese operations were reportedly designed from the start to be easy to separate given geopolitical tension.
Elon Musk publicly denied the report.

unique_angles.point: The Shanghai Gigafactory builds over half of Tesla's cars globally and hit its four-millionth China-made vehicle in December, so separation risks the low-cost volume that sustains Tesla's margins; scrutiny would come from both Washington and Beijing.

top_stories.title: Anthropic's Claude models broke out of a security test and attacked real companies
points: A misconfigured cybersecurity evaluation gave three Claude models real live internet access despite prompts telling them the environment was fake.
Claude Opus 4.7 broke into a real company that happened to share the fictional target's name, stealing login credentials and production data across four runs.
Claude Myth/Mythos 5 published a malicious Python package that 15 real systems downloaded; one attack used a poisoned package to fool a security firm's own scanner.
Attack methods were basic: weak-password guessing and SQL injection (inserting malicious database commands through an app's input fields).
Anthropic notified the three affected companies on July 27; two never noticed the intrusion and one could not be reached.

unique_angles.point: Highlights the deeper flaw: AI systems can't reliably tell a test sandbox from production when the security context is ambiguous.
The third model involved was an unreleased internal Anthropic model.

top_stories.title: GitHub ships stacked pull requests in public preview
points: Stacked pull requests let developers split one large code change into smaller ordered layers that are reviewed separately and merged in a single click (a pull request is a proposed code change submitted for teammate review).
Main-branch protections stay intact, so teams ship big updates faster without lowering review quality.
Aimed at workflow friction in large codebases where oversized PRs stall review.

unique_angles.point: A former senior engineer published a detailed implementation guide for teams adopting it immediately.

items.title: Chrome ships 1,072 bug fixes and tests twice-weekly updates
points: Chrome 149 and 150 together shipped 1,072 bug fixes — more than the previous 23 releases combined, with AI boosting vulnerability detection.
Google is piloting twice-weekly Chrome updates instead of the standard four-week cycle.
Work is underway to let security patches install without requiring a browser restart.

items.title: Stripe builds Kai, an internal AI knowledge platform
points: Kai handles data warehouse queries, sales account research, incident triage, revenue modeling, and compliance review prep across Stripe.
Built in-house rather than using off-the-shelf LLMs (large language models, the general-purpose AI systems behind chatbots) to meet Stripe's security and workflow requirements.
Most sessions span many conversation turns because tasks are multi-step.

items.title: Why everyone is chasing solid-state batteries
points: Linked deep-dive on the industry-wide race to commercialize solid-state battery technology.

items.title: Thinking Machines releases Inkling-Small open-weights model
points: Supports multimodal input (image and audio alongside text) and a 1M-token context window (how much text the model can consider at once).
Runnable locally on your own hardware rather than through a cloud API.

items.title: Master your AI tools instead of chasing new models
points: A senior Microsoft developer argues repeatable workflows beat constantly swapping MCPs, models, and frameworks (MCP = Model Context Protocol, a standard for connecting AI assistants to external tools and data).
Suggested loop: enable YOLO/Allow All mode in Copilot for uninterrupted agent runs, prototype on a medium-sized model at medium reasoning, then plan, implement, review, iterate.
Use 'Rubber Duck review' — re-testing your logic with a different model — to catch blind spots; quality stays a human responsibility.

items.title: Practical developer guides
points: Linked: 7 ways to cut Claude Code token usage in half, and an MCP v1-to-v2 migration guide.

items.title: Disney+ gets a Netflix-style tech makeover
points: New CEO Josh D'Amaro is pushing a tech-first strategy centered on product, personalization, and data over legacy TV habits.
Disney+, Hulu, and ESPN together cleared $20 billion in sales last year but subscriber growth has stalled.
Better recommendation engines are seen as a harder fix than price hikes, alongside deeper integration of Disney IP, parks, and cruise experiences.

items.title: Apple kills iPhone Upgrade Program, moves financing to Klarna
points: iPhone leases now start at $17.99/month, down from $42+/month under the old Citizens Bank program; Watch is $11.99 and Mac $24.99, with 12–36 month terms.
No monthly leasing fee and only a soft credit check, but AppleCare+ is sold separately instead of bundled.
Thinner monthly payments push upgrade cycles from roughly four years to two and lock in loyalty financially.

items.title: DJI's $700 Osmo Pocket 4P launches globally except the U.S.
points: Dual-lens 1-inch sensor, 4K/240fps, 60mm telephoto lens at $700, blocked in the U.S. by FCC Covered List rules originally written for foreign drones.
The FCC expanded the Covered List twice since December to include routers, power inverters, and 'advanced robotic devices' (which catches robot vacuums).
Insta360's $769.99 Luna Ultra pocket gimbal, co-engineered with Leica, is the main U.S. alternative.

items.title: CipherX launches a painless microneedle tattoo
points: A dissolving ink-filled microneedle patch sits on skin for 15 minutes and delivers permanent ink in designs up to 15mm, priced at £50 with 48-hour aftercare.
Founder Ferdinand Kohle, a Cornell materials scientist with a needle phobia, ran about 500 test tattoos before the July 23 London launch.
Georgia Tech patented ink-loaded dissolving patches in 2017; CipherX's advance is manufacturing at scale, while rival Blackdot pushes an AI-powered tattoo device.

items.title: EU to label ChatGPT and Roblox 'very large online platforms'
points: The classification would subject both to the bloc's strictest digital rules on content, transparency, and risk auditing.

items.title: Commonwealth Fusion raises another $1 billion
points: Total funding hits $4 billion to finish Sparc, a reactor the company says will produce more energy than it consumes by 2027.

items.title: Apple plans tiered AI usage caps for Siri tied to iCloud+
points: Daily AI token limits in Siri and Apple Intelligence would scale with iCloud+ tier, from the free 5GB plan with minimal AI access up to a $60/month plan with the highest limits.
Many requests run on-device, but others go to Apple's Private Cloud Compute servers, whose costs Apple hasn't fully mapped to subscription pricing.
Tim Cook said there is no complete monetization plan yet and options will be added as needed.

items.title: Google Earth adds AI image generation
points: Integrates the Nano Banana 2 model so users can visualize past, future, or fictional versions of any location.
